rulings.restated: helper "Anyone on the return made traditional IRA contributions for 2025" = true and helper "You were covered by a retirement plan (1 if Yes)" > 0 (a count)
rulings.model: Coverage comes only from the filer's own work plan or self-employed SEP/SIMPLE. The program has no rule or refusal for the married-filing-separately case, where the instructions say 'If you weren't covered by a retirement plan but your spouse was, you are considered covered by a plan unless you lived apart from your spouse for all of 2025.'
rulings.ruling: Ruling: refusal located elsewhere; project retained. Married filing separately is refused for the whole return before the worksheet is reached: scope.ready refuses on s3.mfs (Form 1040 filing status married filing separately; i1040gi p. 14, Married Filing Separately), so the worksheet's married-filing-separately rule (i1040gi p. 97, "If you weren't covered by a retirement plan but your spouse was, you are considered covered by a plan unless you lived apart from your spouse for all of 2025") is never needed; on the statuses the tool completes, line 1a is the filer's own coverage, as the line asks.

rulings.restated: Add person.ira_se over every confirmed person entry, within the current person when parent-bound. An unanswered roster is unknown.
rulings.model: The refusal properly excludes income where personal services are not "a material income-producing factor." But person.ira_se is undefined, so it cannot be confirmed that it is net self-employment earnings "minus any deductions on Schedule 1, lines 15 and 16" with "If zero or less, enter -0-."
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. person.ira_se is defined per person in forms/2025/person.yaml: the person's Schedule C net profit or loss (person.sc_total) less that person's deductions on Schedule 1 lines 15 and 16 (person.ira_se_take), floored at zero for each person (person.ira_se_figured, the owner's reading amb.2025.ira_se_floor), and zero without a Schedule C; that is i1040gi p. 98, IRA Deduction Worksheet line 9, "Enter the earned income you (and your spouse if filing jointly) received as a self-employed individual or a partner, minus any deductions on Schedule 1, lines 15 and 16. If zero or less, enter -0-". The transcription comparison of person compares these helpers operand by operand; the render glossary does not follow a collection field into its definition (TASKS.md T-055). The new refusal (ira.se_capital_gate) is as the model reads it (p590a pp. 6–7).

rulings.restated: Add person.ira_se over every confirmed person entry, within the current person when parent-bound. An unanswered roster is unknown.
rulings.model: The worksheet says 'Enter the earned income you (and your spouse if filing jointly) received as a self-employed individual or a partner ... If zero or less, enter -0-', applying the floor to the combined amount. The program floors each spouse separately and counts only Schedule C income. The text does not settle whether one spouse's loss nets against the other's earnings, and partnership earned income has no refusal shown here.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: owner ruling (register entry amb.2025.ira_se_floor); project retained. person.ira_se, now shown in the glossary, is each person's Schedule C profit or loss less that person's Schedule 1 lines 15 and 16 deductions, floored at zero per person (i1040gi p. 98, line 9, "Enter the earned income you (and your spouse if filing jointly) received as a self-employed individual or a partner, minus any deductions on Schedule 1, lines 15 and 16. If zero or less, enter -0-"); whether one spouse's loss nets against the other's earnings is the ambiguity the owner settled. Partnership earned income is refused before this line by the Schedule SE screen (person.se_screened, 'partnership and other self-employment income'), so only Schedule C earnings reach it.
